_comment: CCS claim ledger. One record per programme-level claim.
RULE 1: 'status' describes EVIDENCE, not intent, effort, or plausibility.
RULE 2: 'implementation' is a separate axis. Code existing is not evidence.
RULE 3: Any status above 'theoretical-conjecture' requires >=1 evidence entry
pointing at a committed artefact in a sibling repository.
RULE 4: Every claim must name at least one experiment able to FALSIFY it.
RULE 5: Nothing in this file may be restated as a result anywhere in this repo.

claims.title: Three-operator decomposition
claims.statement: Continual-agent competence over a lifetime decomposes usefully into ACCUMULATE (retain candidate experience), ALLOCATE (decide where capacity is assigned), and COMMIT_INTERNAL (decide whether and when a change to durable state is made), with state maintained at multiple timescales. COMMIT_EXTERNAL - releasing an outward response or action - is a distinct commitment domain whose relation to this pipeline is unresolved.
claims.implementation_note: COMMIT machinery exists in state-promotion; an ALLOCATE mechanism now exists in plasticity-routing; a long-horizon ACCUMULATE harness exists in lifetime-integrity. Three of the three existing component tracks state explicitly that they do not assume the decomposition and must not be cited as support for it.
falsified_by: A single-operator or two-operator system matching the full decomposition's performance under identical budgets across every programme benchmark.
Demonstration that ALLOCATE and COMMIT_INTERNAL are not separable, i.e. no experiment can vary one while holding the other fixed.

Demonstration that ACCUMULATE as 'retain candidate experience' and ACCUMULATE as 'continue gathering or thinking' are not the same operator, which would mean the decomposition has been describing two different pipelines under one set of names.
claims.notes: Still a research framing, not a finding. Repository creation is not evidence. Revised 2026-09-03: COMMIT was overloaded, covering both a durable state write and an outward behavioural release. The decomposition above is now explicitly the STATE pipeline and terminates in COMMIT_INTERNAL. Whether COMMIT_EXTERNAL belongs in the same pipeline, runs alongside it, or is governed by a shared principle is tracked as CCS-C12 and is not assumed here. A second, unresolved ambiguity in the same family: this repository has read ACCUMULATE as 'retain candidate experience', while plasticity-routing reads it as 'continue gathering / thinking'. Those are not obviously the same operator, and the second reading is closer to COMMIT_EXTERNAL's WAIT/THINK actions than to state retention. ACCUMULATE has NOT been split, because no track has yet operationalised either reading. modular-consolidation's contamination rules name the decomposition as a conjecture and forbid citing that track as support for it; plasticity-routing scopes itself to ALLOCATE only; lifetime-integrity is architecture-agnostic by construction.

claims.title: Evidence-gated commitment beats scheduled commitment
claims.statement: Under matched trainable-parameter capacity, replay budget, online-token budget and parameter-write ceiling, gating consolidation on already-observed evidence yields lower average forgetting than a fixed or random consolidation schedule, while retaining at least 95% of the strongest baseline's new-task plasticity.
claims.implementation_note: Implemented in state-promotion as arm B5 against B0-B4. Scaffold is pre-result; results/ is empty.

evidence.summary: Toy classifier pilot. Promotion tied with replay within variance (0.457 vs 0.459 final average). The repository states explicitly that this is engineering validation and not evidence for the hypothesis. The fixed-consolidation arm was algebraically identical to replay, so the pilot could not adjudicate the claim at all.

falsified_by: state-promotion/EXP-001 H1 failing under valid, budget-matched conditions.
The promotion arm's advantage disappearing when commit count is matched by the B4 random-routing control (EXP-001 kill criterion 5).
Any observed advantage being attributable to unequal parameter writes, task-identity leakage, or ceiling effects.
claims.notes: Status is 'unresolved' rather than 'pilot-supported': the only pilot returned a null result and its fixed-consolidation arm was degenerate by construction. As of 2026-09-02 main is unchanged at 3495d49 with an empty results/. A sibling records that an off-main small-LM engineering pilot was run and reviewed and was scientifically uninterpretable because the tested soft-prefix plastic representation underlearned, with an architecture-matched LoRA representation-sufficiency repair predeclared. That work is not merged, not on main, and not admissible.

claims.title: Persistent latent state carries context-dependent exceptions
claims.statement: A bounded persistent latent state carried across stream items contributes specifically to handling context-scoped exceptions and reversals, beyond what fast and slow parametric state provide, without materially changing parameter-write volume.
claims.implementation_note: Implemented in state-promotion; the 'promotion-no-latent' ablation is the designated test.
falsified_by: The no-latent and latent-reset ablations matching full B5 on the PALS context/reversal subset.
Any latent-state gain being accompanied by a materially different parameter-write count, which would make it a budget artefact.
claims.notes: This is state-promotion H2. EXP-001 Amendment D architecture-matched latent state across B3/B4/B5 so that the routing comparison is not confounded with latent-state access; that makes the H2 ablation the only clean test of this claim. As of 2026-09-02 main is unchanged at 3495d49 with an empty results/. A sibling records that an off-main small-LM engineering pilot was run and reviewed and was scientifically uninterpretable because the tested soft-prefix plastic representation underlearned, with an architecture-matched LoRA representation-sufficiency repair predeclared. That work is not merged, not on main, and not admissible.

claims.title: Allocation is a separable lever from commitment
claims.statement: Where an experience is routed within the substrate affects the stability-plasticity trade-off independently of when commitment occurs, such that an allocation policy can be varied while holding the commit policy fixed and produce a measurable difference.
claims.implementation_note: plasticity-routing implements a four-action allocator (IGNORE/EPISODIC/FAST/SLOW) over SDW-1, with a 15-feature decision-time whitelist, seven leakage gates, and an exhaustively searched optimal class-to-action mapping.

evidence.summary: DEV_CALIBRATION, trained and evaluated on development seeds {11,12,13}; that track classifies it as not evidence. Two signals point in opposite directions. Kill criterion K1 fired AGAINST learned routing: LEARNED - HEURISTIC = -0.0189, CI [-0.0235,-0.0104], replicating Yoon (2026) in a new setting. K2 did not fire: LEARNED - RANDOM_MATCHED = +0.1108, CI [+0.0927,+0.1264], with a budget-matched control of almost the same action mix, which bears on whether allocation content matters at all. Neither licenses a CCS claim.

falsified_by: Allocation policies producing no measurable difference at fixed commit policy and matched budgets.
Allocation effects being fully explained by the number of commits they induce, which would collapse ALLOCATE into COMMIT.
claims.notes: Status moved from theoretical-conjecture to unresolved because the claim is now implemented and under inconclusive development calibration. This is NOT an evidence promotion: both statuses assert zero empirical support, and the move was not made because a repository appeared. The K1/K2 split matters for how the claim should eventually be read: a learned allocator failing to beat a calibrated fixed rule would not by itself falsify CCS-C4, because CCS-C4 is about allocation being a separable lever, not about the policy being learned. That distinction must be preserved when EXP-001 reads out. Updated 2026-09-03: plasticity-routing froze Protocol v1.0 with no blockers, a pinned commit and source-tree hash, and five held-out confirmatory seeds that have NOT been executed. Its L5a leakage control is retained as permanently failed and non-gating, and the predeclared L5b cross-world attribution gate passed on spent one-shot audit seeds. This is a validity and protocol milestone and adds NO evidence entry here: a frozen protocol is a statement about what may be run, not a result. The claim's status is unchanged and no evidence was recorded.

claims.title: Adaptive consolidation thresholds beat fixed thresholds
claims.statement: For COMMIT_INTERNAL, a consolidation criterion that adapts to observed stream statistics outperforms a well-tuned constant threshold under matched budgets, and does so without requiring held-out evaluation signal.
claims.implementation_note: No implementation. state-promotion deliberately uses a frozen, preregistered threshold, and has not adopted an adaptive-threshold follow-on into its plan of record.
falsified_by: A threshold tuned once on development seeds matching or beating the adaptive policy on confirmatory seeds.
The adaptive policy requiring any held-out or task-identity signal to work, which would make it inadmissible under programme methodology.
claims.notes: Re-scoped 2026-09-03. This claim was previously attached to adaptive-commitment, which was a mischaracterisation: that track is about outward/behavioural commitment timing, not about memory-consolidation thresholds. The claim is retained here as a State Promotion FOLLOW-ON and is now explicitly a COMMIT_INTERNAL claim. It is not owned by adaptive-commitment and must not be cited as that track's motivation. state-promotion has not committed to running it; state-promotion/EXP-F1 is an umbrella-side candidate node, not that track's roadmap. Still only worth testing if CCS-C2 survives: a threshold that adapts is a refinement of a mechanism that must first be shown to matter at all.

claims.title: Modular slow state reduces interference
claims.statement: In an unbounded-capacity regime, consolidating durable knowledge into separable modules produces less cross-task interference than consolidating into a monolithic slow store of equal total capacity.
claims.implementation_note: modular-consolidation implements a generic module lifecycle (allocate, specialise, merge, retire, reinstate) with capacity, cold storage and routing-decision compute all metered.

evidence.summary: Development toy: a fixed bank of the lifecycle's own final size beat the full lifecycle by 7.8 points at identical capacity. Capacity explained the outcome.

Development simulator on a closed-form ridge learner: retention versus capacity is monotone non-decreasing under any competent routing, replicated across three independent mechanisms, so no interior optimum exists. That track draws the consequence that in the unbounded regime at matched capacity consolidation has nothing to fix, and records its own track-local claim 'consolidation beats a capacity-matched fixed bank (unbounded regime)' as falsified. Explicitly not evidence about real models.

falsified_by: Monolithic and modular slow stores showing equal interference at equal capacity and equal write budget on a real model under a frozen protocol.
Modularity gains vanishing once module-selection overhead is charged as decision-time compute.
A fixed bank matched to the dynamic method's own final module count matching or beating it at equal compute.
claims.notes: Held at unresolved rather than falsified, deliberately. The owning track records the unbounded-regime form as falsified in its OWN ledger, but that finding is a development simulator on a closed-form ridge learner, and that track's contamination rule states its results are not evidence for any claim in another track. Promoting a CCS-level status on it would violate both repositories' rules. The claim is NOT rewritten to dodge the negative signal: the unbounded form is kept here with the against-direction evidence attached, and the live constrained question is tracked separately as CCS-C11. Anyone reading CCS-C6 should expect it to end at falsified.
claims.review_by: modular-consolidation/EXP-100 readout, or an admissible real-model test of the unbounded regime

claims.title: Lifetime coherence is maintainable
claims.statement: A multi-timescale substrate can be operated over lifetimes far longer than any single experiment stream without unbounded drift, accumulating commitment error, or monotonically increasing staleness.
claims.implementation_note: lifetime-integrity implements the LIS-v0 generator and nine re-grounding mechanisms behind a metered, capped evidence log, with a corruption lock hashed into every manifest. Architecture-agnostic: any system implementing observe/on_gap/on_context_shift/answer/state_bytes can be scored.

evidence.summary: Single seed, no replication, no confidence intervals, generator still under construction; declared NOT EVIDENCE by that track. Engineering objectives confirmed: budgets bind, audit separation holds, every metric can move, benchmark between floor and ceiling. Provisional orderings recorded against the track's own framing: last-write-wins is hard to beat, and provenance-regrounding does not dominate on integrity despite winning on accuracy. The pilot also suggests mechanisms are near-indistinguishable at 8 epochs and separate by more than 0.25 absolute integrity-violation rate at 128.

falsified_by: Drift, stale-answer rate, or commitment error growing without bound as stream length increases.
Coherence being maintainable only by periodic full resets, which would concede that the substrate does not accumulate.
claims.notes: Status moved to unresolved because a harness and preregistrations now exist, not because anything was shown. A hard external constraint now applies: lifetime-integrity declares itself architecture-agnostic and states that no result from it may be used to claim a CCS latent architecture is validated without an admissible substrate from state-promotion and subsequent routing work. CCS-C7 therefore cannot reach an empirical-support status from that track alone, however strong its results, until state-promotion/EXP-001 reads out admissibly. The pilot's lifetime-length signal, if it replicates, would also mean any short-horizon result in this programme is uninformative about mechanism choice.
claims.review_by: lifetime-integrity/EXP-A001 readout AND an admissible state-promotion substrate

claims.title: The components compose
claims.statement: A system combining accumulation, allocation and commitment outperforms the best single-component system under matched budgets, and the combined gain is not merely the largest individual gain.
claims.implementation_note: No integrated system exists and no repository owns the integration experiment. Per the 2026-09-02 reconciliation instruction, no integration implementation repository is to be created yet.
falsified_by: The integrated system matching but not exceeding the best single component under matched total budget.
Components interfering, so that the combination is worse than its best part.
The combined gain being fully accounted for by one component's contribution.
claims.notes: This is the claim a synthesis paper would exist to make. Four of five component tracks now exist and three have development results, but ccs/EXP-I1 remains undesigned by decision, not by oversight: a non-arbitrary composition test cannot be specified until enough component mechanisms have admissible evidence, and designing it now would bake unsupported component choices into the synthesis programme.

claims.title: Multiple timescales are necessary, not merely sufficient
claims.statement: A single-timescale controller given the same total capacity, write budget and compute cannot match a multi-timescale substrate on the programme's benchmarks.
claims.implementation_note: state-promotion's B1/B2 arms are single-timescale controls for COMMIT. plasticity-routing's ALL_FAST / ALL_SLOW / ALL_EPISODIC single-depth arms are the corresponding controls for ALLOCATE.
falsified_by: A budget-matched single-timescale baseline (B1 or B2) matching the multi-timescale arms on average forgetting and plasticity.
Multi-timescale gains disappearing once decision-time routing compute is added to the total-compute accounting (see CCS-C10).
claims.notes: The programme's own related work already places multi-timescale learning in prior art. This claim is about necessity under matched budgets, which is the only version that is still open. plasticity-routing's development calibration shows every single-depth arm well below its routed arms (best single depth ALL_FAST at 0.230 against LEARNED 0.386), and its K4 criterion would have invalidated the benchmark had a single depth matched. That is a development signal on a synthetic world, not evidence.

claims.title: Gating overhead does not erase the gain
claims.statement: The decision-time inference cost of evidence gating is small enough that the method retains its advantage when compared on total algorithmic compute rather than adaptation compute alone.
claims.implementation_note: state-promotion records decision_forward_calls, decision_tokens_processed and an estimated frozen-backbone decision FLOP proxy separately from adaptation compute.
falsified_by: Gating overhead being large enough that a compute-augmented baseline, given the same total budget, matches the promotion arm.
The performance-vs-total-compute curve showing no region where the promotion arm dominates.
claims.notes: state-promotion Amendment E locked this before results and forbids describing B5 as compute-matched without qualification. This is a genuine falsifier for the practical version of CCS-C2, not a caveat. As of 2026-09-02 main is unchanged at 3495d49 with an empty results/. A sibling records that an off-main small-LM engineering pilot was run and reviewed and was scientifically uninterpretable because the tested soft-prefix plastic representation underlearned, with an architecture-matched LoRA representation-sufficiency repair predeclared. That work is not merged, not on main, and not admissible.

claims.title: Under a binding capacity ceiling, pooling beats destroying
claims.statement: Under a hard capacity ceiling below the number of distinct skills, and at identical live module count, parameters, storage and compute, freeing a slot by pooling modules retains more than freeing it by destroying a module or by refusing to admit a new one.
claims.implementation_note: Implemented in modular-consolidation as the B-MERGE / B-EVICT-LRU / B-DENY arms under an enforced ceiling, with a random-merge control separating the criterion from the rate.

evidence.summary: Development simulator, ceiling 3 with K*=6, 8 paired seeds at identical live-module count, 576 parameters and 33408 bytes of storage per arm. merge - evict = +0.204 retention, CI [+0.125,+0.296]. merge - deny = -0.017 retention with the CI spanning zero, concealing plasticity +0.023 and forgetting +0.039 with CIs excluding zero, i.e. stability converted into plasticity at roughly par. merge - random-merge = +0.009, CI spanning zero, so the pair-selection criterion did not survive to the aggregate. Not evidence about real models.

Preregistered frozen-grid development run (prereg committed before the runner), K* in {6,12,24} x ceiling/K* in {1/6..5/6}, 8 development seeds, 600 rows, 2619 merge events, capacity identical across arms per cell. Construction VALID. SUPPORTS the merge-over-evict half decisively: +0.16 to +0.29 retention with CI excluding zero in every non-degenerate cell. CONTRADICTS the claim's motivating framing on the deny half: merge - deny changes sign with absolute K* rather than with pressure (negative at every non-degenerate ratio for K*=6, positive from ratio 1/3 up for K*>=12), AND within a K* merge's advantage grows as the ceiling LOOSENS, with deny winning at the tightest ratio. Also weakens the third falsifier: the merge criterion separates cleanly from random pairing at K*>=12 (precision 0.45-0.81 vs 0.07-0.19), so EXP-002's weak-coupling observation does not generalise beyond the small-K*, tight-ceiling regime. DEVELOPMENT SEEDS ONLY; no confirmatory seed set drawn; closed-form ridge learner.

falsified_by: merge and evict showing equal retention at an identical binding ceiling under a frozen protocol.
deny matching or beating merge on retention once plasticity is held equal, which would make consolidation a trade rather than a gain.
The advantage over a random-merge control failing to exclude zero, which would mean the rate mattered and the criterion did not.
The merge-over-deny advantage failing to replicate on confirmatory seeds, or remaining confined to a single absolute K*.
claims.notes: Added at the 2026-09-02 reconciliation to keep the live question separate from the unbounded-regime form in CCS-C6, rather than rewriting CCS-C6 to follow the evidence. Two cautions carried from the owning track: 'deny' is a strong and usually-missing baseline that currently leads on retention, and the merge-versus-deny null conceals a significant two-way trade, so a single retention headline would misreport it. Updated 2026-09-03 after EXP-003. Status deliberately UNCHANGED at unresolved: the run used development seeds only and no confirmatory seed set has been drawn, so it is not admissible however well constructed it is. The claim is NOT rewritten to follow the evidence, on the same principle applied to CCS-C6. But the reader should know that its motivating intuition is now under direct pressure: 'under a hard capacity ceiling' was meant to point at high pressure, and high pressure is exactly where the deny half fails - merging needs slack to select well and degenerates when forced. If this survives confirmatory seeds, the honest successor claim is about absolute skill count and selection headroom, not about ceiling tightness. That successor must be ADDED, not substituted.
claims.review_by: a modular-consolidation run on a drawn confirmatory seed set

claims.title: Internal and external commitment share one mechanism
claims.statement: COMMIT_INTERNAL and COMMIT_EXTERNAL are instances of a single commitment principle: one learned mechanism, given the appropriate evidence and cost structure, can govern both when state is made durable and when an outward response is released, and does so at least as well as two domain-specific mechanisms at matched total budget.
claims.implementation_note: Nothing implements this. state-promotion implements COMMIT_INTERNAL only; adaptive-commitment, which would implement COMMIT_EXTERNAL, does not exist. No track implements both, so no track can currently test unification.
falsified_by: The two decisions depending on disjoint evidence, such that no shared policy input space matches domain-specific policies at matched budget.
A shared mechanism underperforming two separate mechanisms at matched total budget in either domain.
Optimal commitment timing in one domain being uncorrelated with the other across streams, which would make the shared principle vacuous even if a shared implementation were possible.

The cost structures proving incommensurable - an internal write costs parameters and interference, an external action costs latency and consequence - such that no single objective expresses both without an arbitrary exchange rate.
claims.notes: Added 2026-09-03 as the explicit, falsifiable home for a unification that the programme's earlier vocabulary asserted by accident. Until 2026-09-03 the umbrella used one word, COMMIT, for both domains, which presupposed this claim rather than testing it. Separating the vocabulary is what makes the claim statable. It is NOT to be treated as a terminology question or as a tidy-up: it is a research hypothesis with a low prior, since the two domains differ in reversibility, cost structure, and who bears the consequence. The last falsifier is the one to watch, because it can hold even if a shared mechanism is buildable.
claims.review_by: adaptive-commitment preregistration, and state-promotion/EXP-001 confirmatory readout
